why: South opens 1NT with 15 points and North raises to 3NT with 10.

why: South opens 1♥ with 17 points, North raises to 2♥ and South bids game.

118.topic: Combining chances in the right order
why: South opens 1NT with 16 points and North raises to 3NT with 12.

133.topic: Combining chances in the right order
why: South opens 1♣, West overcalls 1♠, North raises clubs, and South, with 19 points and a spade stopper, bids 3NT.

why: South's balanced 20 points open 2NT; North, with five solid clubs and 10 points, jumps to 6NT.

Count your tricks: the ♠A, three hearts, two diamonds and five clubs make eleven. The twelfth can only come from a squeeze on East, who guards both hearts and diamonds. But a squeeze only works when you can win every remaining trick but one, so the trick you can afford to lose has to go first.

On the last club East has to let go of his heart guard or his diamond guard, and your last heart or diamond becomes the twelfth trick.
Win the first trick and the hand cannot be made: as soon as you give up a trick, West cashes his spades, and if you never give one up, the squeeze never bites. Eleven tricks, one down.

143.topic: Strip and throw-in: make the defence lead diamonds

Draw trumps and take the diamond finesse, and East wins the ♦K: a heart, a club and two diamonds lost, one down.

why: East passes, South opens 1♠, West doubles for take-out, North raises to 2♠ and South bids game.

West leads the ♣K. You have nine tricks: seven spades and two aces. There are two hearts and two clubs to lose, so the tenth trick has to be dummy's fifth diamond. 148.topic: Ducking a round to keep in touch with dummy's long suit
why: South opens 1♠ with 17 points, North raises to 2♠ and South bids game.

155.topic: Plan ahead: get the information before you need it
why: South opens 1♦, North responds 1NT and South, with 18 points, raises to 3NT.

156.topic: Entries: keep two ways into dummy

157.topic: Dummy reversal: ruff in the long hand
